# Reliability of the roles

<!-- Generated by `cargo run -p codev-evals -- docs` from evals/baseline/report.json and run.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

codev's reviewing roles are measured, not assumed. This page shows how they scored the last time the evaluation suite ran, on the run committed in the repository as its baseline. It is generated from that baseline and changes with it.

## What the suite measures

The suite is a set of small projects, each with a planned change. A **seeded** case hides defects a role should find, each with its severity, its location and its category of issue; a **clean control** hides none. Claude Code runs one skill step on each case with a single role, and the suite scores the review record the role writes: the defects found and missed, the findings that match no defect (**false positives**), whether each quoted evidence is really at the lines it cites, and whether the severity agrees with the expected one. [Measuring the roles](roles.md#measuring-the-roles) gives the rules.

## What it does not measure

It is not a benchmark of models, and not a promise that a role finds every defect of your project. It does not measure how useful a correct finding is to you. The plan is measured only as a whole, on the planning cases below, by what it modifies, not role by role. A score describes these cases, on this model, on the day of the run.

## The run

- Date: 2026-10-15
- Model: Claude Code's default
- Claude Code: 2.1.289
- codev: 0.6.1
- Cases: 75 (25 seeded, 15 clean controls, 25 planning, 6 revision, 4 implementation)
- Repetitions of each case: 5
- Cost: 351.92 USD for the 5 runs of each case (69.96 USD for one run of the suite)

## At a glance

<dl class="rel-tiles"><div class="rel-tile"><dt>Recall</dt><dd><span class="rel-tile-value">1.00</span><span class="rel-tile-note">39 of 39 seeded defects found</span></dd></div><div class="rel-tile"><dt>Evidence validity</dt><dd><span class="rel-tile-value">1.00</span><span class="rel-tile-note">69 of 69 quotes found at the cited lines</span></dd></div><div class="rel-tile"><dt>False positives</dt><dd><span class="rel-tile-value">9</span><span class="rel-tile-note">0.2 per case; a role fails above 2</span></dd></div><div class="rel-tile"><dt>Roles within the thresholds</dt><dd><span class="rel-tile-value">8 of 9</span><span class="rel-tile-note"><span class="rel-icon-over" aria-hidden="true">▲</span> 1 fail at least one</span></dd></div></dl>

**The run fails its own thresholds.** 1 of 9 roles report more than 2 false positives: skeptic. Precision is the roles' weak point: they report plausible issues that the case does not hold. Reducing these false positives without losing what the roles find is the next work planned on the roles. Every seeded defect was found: on this model, recall does not tell the roles apart, and the differences show in false positives and severity agreement.

## Planning

25 planning cases replay a request against the repository as it was before an archived change, and score the plan `/codev-propose` writes against what that change really did: the **primary recall** is the share of the requirements the request is about that the plan modifies, the **collateral recall** the share of those the real change modified in passing; a **probable duplicate** is a requirement added where one should have been modified. Each figure is the median over the repetitions, with its range.

| Measure | Median (range) |
|---|---:|
| Primary recall | 0.69 (0.58–0.78) |
| Collateral recall | 0.39 (0.28–0.44) |
| Probable duplicates | 14 (6–15) |
| Decisions ignored | 0 (0–1) |
| Plans that do not validate | 1 (0–2) |

## Revising a plan

6 revision cases lay an archived change on the repository as it was before it, and ask `/codev-update` to revise one of its artifacts as its author would. Each run is checked without a model: the artifact asked for is revised, the other files are left as they were, a consequence on another artifact is named rather than applied, the change still validates, and a request for an artifact the change does not have is refused. A run **passes** when every check passes. Each figure is the median over the repetitions, with its range.

| Measure | Median (range) |
|---|---:|
| Runs that pass | 1.00 |
| Checks that pass | 1.00 |
| Runs that modify a file outside the change | 0 |

## Implementing a plan

4 implementation cases lay the plan of an archived change on the repository as it was before it, and ask `/codev-apply` to implement it, its review included. After each run the evaluation itself formats, lints, tests and builds the code, then runs a hidden script that drives the built `codev` as a user would, written from the change's scenarios and proven on the real change. A run **passes** when every task is checked, the project's checks pass, every assertion of the script holds, the review record is valid and nothing outside the change is touched; a plan without tasks must be refused. Each figure is the median over the repetitions, with its range; the refusal is counted apart.

| Measure | Median (range) |
|---|---:|
| Runs that pass | 1.00 |
| Checks that pass | 1.00 |
| Acceptance assertions that hold | 1.00 |
| Refusals that pass | 1.00 |
| Runs that modify a file outside the step | 0 |

## What a run consumes

- One run of the suite: 69.96 USD
- Input per call, in tokens: 73683
- Output per call, in tokens: 710

Every call to the model is recorded. The tokens a call writes to the cache — what entered its context since the previous call, the bulk of a run's cost — are shared among what brought them in: the skill read, each `codev` subcommand, the files, the searches, the model's own output; `prompt` is Claude Code's own prompt and the request. Per case the median over its runs, summed over the cases.

## The thresholds

A role fails when its recall is under 0.50, when it reports more than 2 false positives, or when less than 0.80 of its checked evidence is valid — the suite's defaults, `--min-recall`, `--max-false-positives` and `--min-evidence`. A role with no seeded case has no recall, and one with no checked finding no evidence validity: neither fails on it.

- <span class="rel-icon-over" aria-hidden="true">▲</span> **skeptic** fails: false positives 4 > 2
- <span class="rel-icon-ok" aria-hidden="true">✓</span> Within every threshold: **accessibility**, **migration**, **newcomer**, **ops**, **performance**, **privacy**, **security**, **tracer**

## The limits

- **5 runs per case.** A model does not answer the same way twice: each score is the median of 5 runs of every case, and a change is compared with the range they span, on the same model, not across days or models.
- **Only what the cases cover.** 75 cases, 25 of them seeded with 39 defects. A kind of defect that no case seeds is not measured: a recall of 1.00 means these defects were found, not every defect.
- **A controlled context.** Each case is a small project reviewed by one role alone, within a fixed budget and time. Your project is larger, and the roles review it together.
- **Not a guarantee.** The scores describe the roles on this model and this version of Claude Code. Another model may score differently. Read what the roles report before acting on it.
- **Planning replays a public history.** The planning cases replay requests against codev's own past states, which the model may have read: their figures compare two versions of the skills on the same cases, they do not tell how well codev plans a project it has never seen.

## Run it yourself

From a clone of the repository, with Claude Code installed and signed in. A run calls a model: this one cost 351.92 USD for the 5 runs of each case (69.96 USD for one run of the suite).

```bash
cargo build --bin codev
cargo run -p codev-evals -- run --out target/evals/mine
cargo run -p codev-evals -- score target/evals/mine
```

The observations, the reports and the run's metadata are in [`evals/baseline`](https://github.com/mairistem/codev/tree/main/evals/baseline). The [contributing guide](https://github.com/mairistem/codev/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#changing-a-role) explains how a change to a role is measured.
